name: Cycubix
one_line: A Dublin cybersecurity and GRC consultancy and training company; its first product, ConsentScan, scans websites for cookie and consent violations, with an MCP server on its Pro plan.

facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: Cycubix offers cybersecurity training (secure coding in several languages, threat modeling, secure coding for AI and LLM applications against the OWASP Top 10 for LLMs) and consultancy (risk reviews, ISO 27001, GDPR, SOC, NIS2, vCISO).

facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: ConsentScan, by Cycubix Ltd, Dublin, is a GDPR and ePrivacy cookie consent checker: one free scan with no sign-up, about 4 minutes, graded A to F.

facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: A scan loads the site like a first-time EU visitor, records what fires before consent, then clicks Reject and checks whether trackers keep firing.

facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: ConsentScan started as a check Cycubix ran during its ISO 27001, GDPR and security engagements.

facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: Plans: Free (1 scan); Starter €19 a month (1 monitored domain); Pro €39 a month (3 monitored domains, and an MCP server to run scans from Claude, Cursor or any MCP client); Agency €99 (10 domains); Enterprise on request.

facts.label: From their own pages
facts.fact: Its EU Consent Index (2 Nov 2026) tested 160 leading websites in eight EU countries: 69% loaded trackers or non-essential cookies before consent, and 58% of the sites where a Reject click could be completed kept tracking afterwards.

told: Both sides agreed the public company information can be published as a case study.

help.label: Our hypothesis, not their claim. Built from public pages only; nothing of theirs was tested.
help.pitch: ConsentScan measures the gap between what a site says (its consent banner) and what it does (the trackers that fire). RiskMandate measures the same kind of gap for AI agents: what an agent was asked to do against what it can reach. For ConsentScan's own agentic workflow and its MCP server, RiskMandate would write down the mandate, measure the reach and record the gap.

mandate.text: The scanner's own job: load a site, record cookies, click Reject, grade. A narrow, writable mandate.

reach.text: Its MCP server lets Claude, Cursor or any MCP client run scans: an outside agent with a tool. What the MCP server's credentials can reach beyond scanning is unknown from public pages.

gap.text: Unknown from public pages; the mandate is narrow, so the gap is measurable. 'Installed, not blocking' (its words for consent platforms) is the same shape as an agent policy that exists but is not enforced.

together.label: Our suggestions. Nothing here is agreed.
